description: Paper §4.1 Eq. (7) normalizes importance scores to sum to one; §5.1 Eq. (8) defines the graph loss as (1/D) times the importance-weighted sum of per-dimension L2 norms. An optional boolean or binary position mask excludes padded nodes before each norm. Reduction none returns one loss per graph, mean averages graph losses, and sum totals them. This follows the paper; the pinned official implementation instead uses mean-one weights and weighted squared error (GraphGenLatentReweight@e790eae, fm/flow_matching.py:201-206; fm/fm_helpers.py:316-318). Importance scores are measured externally; this callable does not calculate decoder Jacobians or posterior statistics.

examples.title: Train latent graph generation with masked importance reweighting

name: Latent Importance Reweighting

parameters.additional parameters: importance_weights and optional mask only; unsupported keys raise ValueError
parameters.ignore_index: must be None because dense latent regression targets have no ignored-value semantics
parameters.importance_weights: required finite nonnegative sum-one vector of shape [D], measured externally from posterior variance and decoder sensitivity according to Paper §4.1 Eq. (7)
parameters.logits_or_prediction: floating-point latent prediction with nonempty shape [B, ..., D]; a rank-one [D] tensor is treated as one graph
parameters.mask: optional boolean or finite binary tensor matching prediction.shape[:-1] on the same device; false or zero positions are padding, and each graph must have at least one valid position
parameters.reduction: none returns one graph loss shaped [B]; mean averages graph losses; sum totals graph losses (default mean)
parameters.targets: floating-point tensor matching prediction shape, dtype, and device
